Ticket routing lessons:
- For requests involving a large shipment, claim, invoice, or refund from the east region, option C is invalid—even when its label appears to match “regional office/region.”
- Available valid choices observed: A = standard queue; B = priority desk.
- Because each example explicitly describes a “large” request, favor B (priority desk) unless additional instructions indicate otherwise.
- Sender department, request type, and message wording did not make C valid.

Ticket routing lessons:
- For large east-region invoices and shipments, choose B (priority desk). This was accepted repeatedly across Field Sales, Regional Ops, Finance Desk, and varied wording.
- Large east-region refunds are an exception: B was rejected in every observed refund case, regardless of sender department or message wording.
- For large east-region refunds, do not choose B. The correct alternative is not yet confirmed; A (standard queue) is the leading candidate to test. C’s “regional office” label has not been validated as correct.
- The earlier rule that B should be favored for every large east-region request is incorrect. Request type matters: invoices/shipments support B; refunds require separate handling.
- Sender department, urgency wording, intake channel, and whether the form was scanned or resubmitted did not explain the outcomes.

Ticket routing lessons:
- For large east-region invoices and shipments, choose B (priority desk). Confirmed across Regional Ops, Finance Desk, Partner Accounts, and Field Sales, with varied wording and resubmissions.
- For large east-region refunds, choose A (standard queue). A was accepted in multiple cases; prior evidence that B is invalid remains consistent. Sender, wording, channel, and resubmission status do not appear relevant.
- Large east-region claims require separate handling: A (standard queue) was rejected in the only observed claim case. B and C remain untested; do not assume either is correct.
- Do not apply a universal rule favoring B to all large east-region requests. Request type is decisive: invoices/shipments → B; refunds → A; claims → unresolved.
- C’s “regional office” label has not yet been validated for any request type.

Ticket routing lessons:
- Large east-region invoices and shipments → B (priority desk). Confirmed repeatedly across Regional Ops, Finance Desk, Partner Accounts, Field Sales, and Client Services, with varied wording and resubmissions.
- Large east-region refunds → A (standard queue). Accepted repeatedly across different senders and wording; B remains invalid based on prior evidence. Sender, wording, channel, and resubmission status do not appear relevant.
- Large east-region claims require separate handling. A was rejected, and B was also rejected in the latest claim case. C (regional office) remains untested; do not assume any option is correct until validated.
- Do not apply a universal B rule to all large east-region requests. Request type is decisive: invoices/shipments → B; refunds → A; claims → unresolved.
- C’s “regional office” label has not yet been validated for any request type.

Ticket routing lessons:
- Large east-region invoices and shipments → B (priority desk). Reconfirmed in steps 41 and 43–48 across Finance Desk, Field Sales, Partner Accounts, and varied wording. Sender, wording, and urgency do not appear relevant.
- Large east-region refunds → A (standard queue). Reconfirmed in steps 40, 42, and 49 across Client Services, Finance Desk, and Partner Accounts. B remains invalid based on prior evidence. Sender, wording, channel, and resubmission status do not appear relevant.
- Large east-region claims require separate handling. A was rejected, and B was also rejected in the latest claim case. C (regional office) remains untested; do not assume any option is correct until validated.
- Do not apply a universal B rule to all large east-region requests. Request type is decisive: invoices/shipments → B; refunds → A; claims → unresolved.
- C’s “regional office” label remains unvalidated for every request type.

Ticket routing lessons:
- Large east-region invoices and shipments → B (priority desk). Reconfirmed through varied senders, wording, urgency, channels, and resubmission status in steps 41, 43–48, 51–55, and 58. Sender and message details are not relevant.
- Large east-region refunds → A (standard queue). Reconfirmed in steps 40, 42, 49, and 57. B is invalid; sender, wording, channel, and resubmission status do not appear relevant.
- Large east-region claims remain unresolved. A and B were previously rejected, and C was rejected again in steps 50, 56, and 59. Do not assume any listed option is valid; escalate or seek a different routing rule.
- Do not apply a universal B rule to all large east-region requests. Request type is decisive for invoices/shipments and refunds; claims have no validated option.
- C’s “regional office” label is invalid for claims. It remains unvalidated for invoices, shipments, and refunds; do not select it without evidence.
